newsitem.title: FRANCE: French diplomat abducted in Yemen said freed.
newsitem.headline: French diplomat abducted in Yemen said freed.

text.p: Yemeni tribesmen released on Friday a French diplomat they had held for 11 days and then retook within hours of releasing him a first time last Sunday, French radio said.
The radio gave no details. A French Foreign Ministry spokesman could not immediately confirm the report.
The unnamed diplomat was abducted by al-Toaiman tribesmen demanding jobs, settlement of a land dispute and compensation for losses to homes and farms in floods that killed 65 people last June.
He was kidnapped as he drove his car in Sanaa, and was held in Marib province, 170 km (100 miles) north of the Yemeni capital.
The tribesmen released him last Sunday, but recaptured him and his escort within hours as they were returning to Sanaa.
Yemeni authorities say the diplomat, whom Paris has declined to identify, is a first secretary at the embassy.

At least two diplomats, a Saudi ambassador and an American, have been among foreigners and tourists kidnapped in recent years and used as bargaining chips by Yemeni tribesmen pressing mostly non-political grievances against the government.
There has been no report of casualties from the abductions.
